match.reason: The closest bank point, ecb-ways-earn-income, is a broader overview of all income types (wages, profit, dividends, rent, government payments), while the new point teaches the specific wage-versus-salary distinction, so no bank point teaches the same idea at the right depth.

draft.title: Wages and salaries
card: Income is money a person receives. Money earned from working for an employer is called income from employment.
money paid for each hour worked. A worker who does more hours earns more, and one who does fewer hours earns less.
a fixed amount for a whole year, paid in equal parts, such as every fortnight. It stays the same even if the hours worked change a little from week to week.
Wages and salaries are both income from employment. They differ in how the pay is worked out.
draft.remember: Wage: paid by the hour. Salary: a yearly amount paid in parts.

a.q: Jai is paid $26 for every hour he works at a pool. What is this pay called?
a.why: Jai is paid for each hour he works, so his pay is a wage. A salary is a fixed yearly amount paid in parts, which does not match pay worked out by the hour.
a.clue: Look at how his pay is worked out.

b.q: Priya works as an office manager in Geelong. Her contract says she earns $78,000 a year, paid in equal amounts each fortnight. Why is this a salary?
opts: It is a fixed yearly amount, paid in parts
It is paid for each hour she works
It is not income from employment
It changes with the hours she works each week
b.why: A salary is a fixed amount for a year, paid in parts, and Priya's pay fits this. Being paid every fortnight does not make it a wage, because a wage is worked out for each hour worked.
b.clue: Think about how the yearly amount is split up.

b.best: It is a fixed yearly amount, paid in parts
